thread:
maria: Heads up — seeing a sustained throughput drop on dedicated-pool-3 since ~10:05 UTC and multiple worker restarts. Topline: tokens/sec down ~35%, tail latency spikes. link: https://grafana.redwood/boards/abcd :warning:
ken: on it. any obvious OOMs in node logs?
jp: I see worker restarts in kube events, reason: OOMKilled for runtime-worker. 3/12 pods restarted in last 7m.
maria: stack trace from one worker attached below (trimmed):
```
RuntimeError: GPU allocation failed: CUDA out of memory
  at allocate_kv_cache (serve/runtime/mem.cc:243)
  at KernelSelector::evict_or_fallback (serve/runtime/kernel_selector.cc:112)
  at Worker::process_request (serve/worker/worker.cc:511)
```
nia: interesting — recent rollout of kernel-selection heuristic v2 landed ~09:50 UTC (infra-bot deploy note). @infra-bot can you confirm?
infra-bot: deploy:kernel-selection/v2 rolled to dedicated-pool-3 at 2025-10-04T09:50:12Z by thomas. changelog: adapt kernel choice based on observed batch footprints and quantization availability. :package:
jp: profiling snapshot (nsys) shows a sudden increase in device memory high-water mark when small-batch requests hit a fallback kernel path. snippet:
```
GPU mem highwater: 11.9 GB -> 14.7 GB
kernel: aten::matmul_fallback (unquantized) used for 62% of small batches
kv_cache_reserve: +2.6GB per active stream
```
thomas: Oof. That matches a theory: new heuristic prefers lower-latency unquantized kernel for tiny batches but that kernel allocs a larger temp buffer, causing kv cache pressure and eviction churn. On multi-tenant noisy nodes that kicks memory over threshold.
ken: is eviction thrash causing many small KV re-loads and making requests heavier? Any evidence of repeated KV misses?
maria: yes, from tracer logs: pattern of repeated prefix cache evictions and reloads for same keys within ~20s window. count: 87 evict/reload cycles for a single session.
nia: so cascade: kernel selection -> higher per-request scratch mem -> KV evictions -> reloads bump mem and IO -> OOM -> kube restarts -> throughput drop.
jp: quick mitigation: can we pin kernel-selection to v1 on pool-3? rollback would be fastest. Also we can disable the unquantized fallback lane.
thomas: I can push a targeted rollback to dedicated-pool-3 now. doing `infra deploy rollback kernel-selection v1 --target dedicated-pool-3`
infra-bot: rollback initiated by thomas at 2025-10-04T10:03:02Z.
ken: re: long-term fix: need to adjust heuristic to account for KV cache marginal cost and to prefer quantized kernels when KV pressure > threshold. Also add unit to test that simulates small-batch-heavy KV eviction to catch regressions.
maria: agree. also add a safety circuit: if device mem high-water > 90% trigger kernel fallback to lower-memory kernel, rather than unquantized one.
nia: I ran a perf replay locally with v2 but with KV cache disabled — memory looks fine. With KV enabled it regresses. So heuristic must be KV-aware. I'll open a perf issue with repro and nsys traces.
jp: after rollback, we should see pods stabilize. current pod restarts 3 -> 0 over next few minutes expected. i'll keep monitoring.
thomas: follow-up tasks: 1) revert v2 from global rollout until KV-aware changes done 2) add regression test 3) add observability metric for kernel-chosen vs mem-hwm 4) consider making kernel selection stateful per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbor flips.
maria: noted. can we add an immediate mitigation to throttle small concurrent KV reloads? maybe a short debounce on eviction to avoid repeated re-load storms.
ken: good idea. also add rate limit on placement of new small batches to same GPU if recent eviction observed.
sre-oncall: incident page started: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20251004-1 — updating with rollback and root-cause hypothesis.
jp: pods are reporting healthy again, throughput recovering to ~98% of baseline at 10:18 UTC. I'll let this sit and collect traces for the postmortem.
maria: thanks team. assign owners: nia -> perf repro + issue, thomas -> rollback + rollout policy change, ken -> test + threshold logic, jp -> postmortem & monitoring updates.
ken: I'll draft the PR for KV-aware heuristic adjustments and the new tests.
maria: great. adding notes: retro checklist: include synthetic noisy-tenant test, kernel memory accounting in allocator, and safe-mode flag for kernel-selection. closing thread when postmortem + PRs linked. :white_check_mark:
